# refactor(domain): move shared failure helpers into a failures owner

One slice of the application-boundaries refactor. **Treat this request as self-contained**:
everything needed is below and in `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`. Do not assume access to
any other issue or pull request.

Lands before the issue that assigns error classes to their owners; that issue builds on this one.

## What

The small pieces of code that describe a failure and retry a failed step get a home of their own.
Users see the same messages, and the same steps are retried the same number of times.

## Why

Those pieces live with the business rules today, although they are not business rules. They are
used from almost every part of jig, and no other existing place can be reached from all of those
parts. Giving them one dedicated place lets the business rules stay pure.

## Context — read this first

jig is a TypeScript CLI that turns a markdown request into planned slices, has agents implement and
review each one in a sandbox, and lands them on one run branch. Source owners under `src/`:
`domain` (business rules), `ports` (external capability contracts), `config` (settings schemas and
policy), `flow`/`steps` (workflow execution), `prompts`, `observers` (events and reporting),
`adapters` (Git, files, containers, terminal, logging), `integrations/github`, `app` (use cases)
and `cli` (commands). Specs sit beside the code they cover (`foo.ts` → `foo.spec.ts`). Before
editing, read `AGENTS.md`, the house rules in `.claude/rules/` that cover the files you change, and
`docs/architecture.html`.

Read these sections of `docs/specs/application-boundaries.md`: "Target responsibilities" (the
owner table and the `failures` paragraphs below it) and "Error ownership and technical failure
handling". Where this issue and the spec disagree, follow the spec and say so in the PR.

## Target

A new owner, `src/failures/`. It imports no project source; it depends only on `better-result` and
Node. Callers import its functions directly.

Move these, with their specs, and change nothing about how they behave:

| Today | Moves to | Consumers today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `messageOf` in `src/domain/errors.ts` | `src/failures/messages.ts` | adapters (filesystem, find-symlink, git, local-store, run-store, sandbox-image, sandcastle, terminal), `app/init-sandbox.ts`, `app/run-stores.ts`, `app/sandbox-image.ts`, `cli/read-request.ts`, `cli/with-error-handling.ts`, `flow/engine.ts`, `observers/run-events.ts`, `integrations/github` |
| `rootCause` in `src/domain/errors.ts` | `src/failures/messages.ts` | `flow/engine.ts`, `cli/with-error-handling.ts` |
| `retryResult`, `RetryPolicy` in `src/domain/retry.ts` | `src/failures/retry.ts` | `adapters/git/remote-ref.ts`, `app/container.ts`, `flow/engine.ts`, `steps/planning.ts`, `integrations/github/octokit-github.ts`, `integrations/github/orchestration-store.ts` |

Grep for each name before you start; the table is a starting point, not a substitute.

Stays in `domain`, untouched by this issue: every error class, `JigError`, `FailureKind`,
`isTransient`, `isJigError`, and `transientRetryPolicy`. `transientRetryPolicy(settings)` reads
`RunSettings` and returns `{ retries, delayMs, shouldRetry: isTransient }`. Domain must not import
`failures`, so type its result structurally in `src/domain/retry.ts`; it still satisfies
`RetryPolicy` at the call site. A separate issue moves the error classes; do not start that here.

`retryResult` stays a hand-written wrapper. better-result 3.0.1's retry exists only inside
`Result.tryPromise`, which retries a rejected promise. jig operations return `Result` values and
never throw, and callers need `onFailedAttempt` on every failed attempt, the last one included.
Keep exactly this: the first attempt runs at once; `onFailedAttempt({ error, attempt, retriesLeft })`
runs before the retry decision, including the final and non-retryable attempt; the delay is
`delayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`; the last `Err` is returned. Never throw an `Err` to reach a library
retry loop. Say this in the PR as the reason for the wrapper.

## Dependency rules

Policy lives in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs`, with fixtures in
`scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`. Do not write another source scanner.

- Add `failures` to `productionModules` in `.dependency-cruiser.mjs`.
- `failures` imports nothing under `src/` outside `src/failures/`.
- `domain`, `ports`, `config` and `prompts` do not import `failures`.
- Every other owner may import it. `integrations/github` keeps its current imports until the GitHub
  issue moves it.
- Add a passing and a failing fixture for each rule.

## Don't undo these

- **No port, adapter or injection for these helpers.** Do not add `src/ports/retry.ts`,
  `src/ports/exception-details.ts` or adapter implementations of them, and do not pass them through
  constructors, dependency objects or the container. They are pure functions (plus a timer); a
  direct import is the design.
- Do not change construction or wiring in `src/app/container.ts` beyond its import paths. The
  construction mechanism is decided separately.
- No compatibility re-exports from `src/domain/errors.ts` or `src/domain/retry.ts`. Update every
  caller.
- Agents run unattended only inside the sandbox. Never add an agent call that runs on the host.
- Credentials never land in a file jig writes, a log line or the image.
- Nothing touches the target repository's tracked files outside the run's worktree.
- Keep commands, flags, defaults, help, error tags and messages, exit codes, configuration
  precedence and recovery behavior unchanged.
- Expected failures are `Result` values; bugs panic. jig never throws.
- Change only what this issue needs. Leave unrelated specs and assertions as they are.
- No release tags and no version bumps; `main` publishes on its own.

## Documentation

Internal-only work: no public guide changes. Update these references in place, present tense:

- `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`: the paths for `rootCause` and `retryResult`, and the
  paragraph that says the panic helpers live in `src/domain/errors.ts`.
- `docs/architecture.html`: the failure-policy card that names `retryResult` and `domain`, plus
  any owner list.
- `docs/workflow-ownership.md`: import lines that now point at `failures/`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: add `src/failures/` to the code map.

## How to work

From the repository root, with Node 26.13.0:

```sh
npm run lint:dependencies
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation
```

## Done when

- [ ] `git grep -n -E "export (async )?function (messageOf|rootCause|retryResult)" src` finds them
      only under `src/failures/`
- [ ] `git grep -n "from '.*failures/" src/domain src/ports src/config src/prompts` finds nothing
- [ ] `src/ports/retry.ts` and `src/ports/exception-details.ts` do not exist
- [ ] the specs for `messageOf`, `rootCause` and `retryResult` pass from their new location, with
      the same cases as before
- [ ] `npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation` passes from the repository root
- [ ] the PR names `failures` as the owner, says why these helpers belong there, and says it is a
      one-off: new helpers go to the module whose rule they express, not here by habit

docs.design:
# Goal

Move failure presentation, panic unwrapping and Result-based retry execution into `src/failures/`, preserving every observable behavior and retry budget. Keep business classification and settings-based retry policy in domain.

# Context

`src/domain/errors.ts` currently owns error classes, `JigError`, `FailureKind`, `isTransient` and `isJigError`, alongside two technical helpers: `messageOf` renders an `Error` message or `String(value)`, and `rootCause` unwraps nested better-result panics. Its colocated spec mixes helper cases with classification and error-class cases.

`src/domain/retry.ts` currently owns both generic retry execution (`retryResult`, `RetryPolicy`) and business policy (`transientRetryPolicy`). The latter reads `RunSettings`, selects `isTransient`, and currently types its return through `Omit<RetryPolicy<JigError>, 'onFailedAttempt'>`. Its spec mixes generic retry cases, policy cases and one integration case combining the two.

The source inventory confirms consumers in adapters, app, CLI, flow, observers, steps and integrations/github. `flow/engine.ts` combines domain policy with retry execution and uses both message helpers. `app/container.ts` also combines policy and execution while constructing sandbox sessions. Config filesystem adapters are message-helper consumers; config itself is not.

`.dependency-cruiser.mjs` registers eleven production owners and defines dependency restrictions. `scripts/check-dependencies.mjs` discovers production files, enforces ownership, checks module cycles including type imports, and separately checks runtime file cycles. Its colocated spec runs the real checker against temporary source trees. Existing domain, ports and config restrictions already prohibit their importing a future failures owner; prompts needs an explicit restriction.

The application-boundaries spec assigns these technical mechanisms to failures because no existing owner is reachable by all consumers without violating ownership. The house rules require callee-owned rules, expected failures as Result values, preservation of bug propagation, and library reuse unless a wrapper has a concrete justification. Test changes follow the colocated-spec and setup conventions while preserving existing cases and unrelated assertions.

# Chosen approach

Create `src/failures/messages.ts` containing the existing `messageOf` and `rootCause` implementations, and `src/failures/retry.ts` containing the existing `RetryPolicy` and `retryResult`. Use direct imports with the repository's ESM `.js` specifiers. Add no barrel, compatibility exports, ports, adapters or injection.

Keep every error class, union, classification and recognition function in domain. Keep `transientRetryPolicy` and its exported `TransientRetryPolicy` type in `src/domain/retry.ts`, replacing the type's dependency on `RetryPolicy` with the structural shape `{ retries: number; delayMs: number; shouldRetry(error: JigError): boolean }`. This preserves compatibility at existing call sites without creating a domain-to-failures edge.

Preserve retry execution exactly: attempt one runs immediately; every returned Err invokes `onFailedAttempt({ error, attempt, retriesLeft })` before the retry decision, including exhausted and non-retryable attempts; delays are `delayMs * 2 ** (attempt - 1)`; success or the final Err is returned unchanged; rejected bugs propagate. Keep the handwritten wrapper because better-result 3.0.1 retries rejected promises within `Result.tryPromise`, whereas these operations return Result values and require terminal-attempt callbacks. Never throw an Err to use library retry.

Move helper cases into `failures/messages.spec.ts` and `failures/retry.spec.ts`. Leave classification, error-class and standalone policy cases beside domain. Move the existing policy/execution integration case into `flow/engine.spec.ts`, a consumer-owned spec permitted to import both owners. Preserve its settings-budget assertion and all existing helper cases without introducing cross-owner imports into domain or failures specs.

Register failures in `productionModules`. Extend the existing Dependency Cruiser policy to allow production failures imports only from itself, better-result and Node, rejecting other source owners and external packages. Same-owner imports remain subject to existing cycle checks. Reuse domain, ports and config restrictions and add the missing prompts-to-failures prohibition. Other existing owners, including integrations/github, may import failures. Test packages remain outside the production dependency allowlist's scope. Use the existing checker and fixtures; no additional scanner is needed.

The current architecture differs from the target because technical helpers live in domain and failures is absent from the owner registry. This change resolves those differences. The full spec also redistributes error classes, introduces composition and removes integrations; those are staged migrations outside this request. Retain current error ownership, integrations/github placement and container construction, changing only relevant imports. Record this staging in the eventual PR rather than applying the full target architecture prematurely. There is no disagreement on the helper extraction itself.

Update the four named internal references in place. Describe failures as a one-off shared technical owner: future helpers belong to the module whose rule they express, not here by habit.

# Alternatives considered

1. **Keep the helpers in domain or move them into flow/adapters.** Rejected because they express technical mechanisms rather than business rules, and neither flow nor adapters is available to all current consumers under the dependency rules.
2. **Introduce retry and exception-details ports with injected implementations.** Rejected because these functions need only better-result and a timer. Injection adds contracts and wiring without a capability boundary, contradicting the explicit direct-import design.
3. **Replace the loop with better-result retry.** Rejected because its rejected-promise retry does not preserve returned-Err handling and the required callback on every failed attempt. Converting Err values into rejections would violate the failure model.

# Assumptions

- The implementation checkout supplies the same helper contracts and mixed specs inspected here; refresh the symbol inventory before editing.
- The dependency allowlist constrains production code, while colocated specs may use Vitest and faker under the existing checker exclusions.
- Node 26.13.0 is used for implementation validation. This design-only step does not run validation or modify files.
- No public interface changes result, so public usage guides need no edits.

# Non-goals

Error-class redistribution; changes to tags, fields, classification or messages; new retry behavior or defaults; container construction changes; composition or GitHub migration; new helper abstractions; unrelated test cleanup; public guide additions; version bumps or release tags. Sandbox-only agent execution, credential handling and target-worktree isolation remain unchanged.

# Affected areas

- New `src/failures/messages.ts`, `messages.spec.ts`, `retry.ts` and `retry.spec.ts`.
- `src/domain/errors.ts`, `errors.spec.ts`, `retry.ts` and `retry.spec.ts`; `src/flow/engine.spec.ts` for the existing integration case.
- Discovered helper imports throughout adapters, app, CLI, flow, observers, steps and integrations/github. `src/app/container.ts` changes imports only.
- `.dependency-cruiser.mjs` and `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts`; the existing checker remains the enforcement mechanism without requiring new scanning logic.
- `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`, `docs/architecture.html`, `docs/workflow-ownership.md` and `CONTRIBUTING.md`.
docs.plan:
## Step 1 — Confirm the extraction boundary

Read `AGENTS.md`, applicable house rules, the architecture map and the specified application-boundaries sections. Search all source and specs for `messageOf`, `rootCause`, `retryResult`, `RetryPolicy` and `transientRetryPolicy`; inventory mixed imports and current test cases. Confirm the pinned Node 26.13.0 environment. Treat the helper extraction, consumer migration and preserved behavior as one coherent refactor.

## Step 2 — Extract the helpers with their consumers and tests

Create `src/failures/messages.ts` and `src/failures/retry.ts` by moving the existing implementations and generic policy interface without algorithm changes. Remove their original exports and unused imports from domain. Retain all domain error definitions and classification behavior, and give `TransientRetryPolicy` an equivalent structural type independent of failures.

Update every inventoried consumer to import directly from failures, splitting imports where domain symbols remain necessary. Keep `transientRetryPolicy` imports in domain. Change only imports in `src/app/container.ts`; preserve all construction and wiring.

Move message and panic-unwrapping cases into `failures/messages.spec.ts`, and generic retry cases into `failures/retry.spec.ts`. Keep domain-only cases in their existing specs. Relocate the policy/execution budget case into `flow/engine.spec.ts` with its existing behavior and assertions, avoiding domain-to-failures and failures-to-domain imports. Run the affected helper, domain and consumer specs. Review the moved implementation for immediate first execution, callback ordering including terminal failures, exponential delay, final Err identity and rejected-bug propagation.

## Step 3 — Enforce the owner boundary through the existing checker

Add failures to `productionModules`. Add production dependency rules allowing failures to import only itself, better-result and Node, and prohibiting prompts from importing failures. Keep existing domain, ports and config restrictions and preserve integrations/github's other current edges. Do not add a scanner or broaden unrelated owner policies.

Extend `scripts/check-dependencies.spec.ts` with passing and failing fixtures for every new boundary. Cover same-owner imports, better-result and Node as allowed; other source owners and other external packages as rejected; imports into failures from every permitted current owner as allowed; and imports from domain, ports, config and prompts as rejected. Exercise runtime and type-only edges, assert the relevant rule diagnostics, retain production/spec exclusion behavior, and update the all-owners discovery fixture to include failures. Preserve existing ownership and cycle coverage. Run the checker specs and `npm run lint:dependencies`.

## Step 4 — Update internal ownership references

Update rootCause and retryResult paths and the current-layout paragraph in `.claude/rules/errors-as-values.md`, distinguishing the extracted helpers from the error classes still in domain. Update the failure-policy card and affected owner/dependency representations in `docs/architecture.html`, keeping retry execution distinct from domain classification and engine decisions.

Update affected import lines and current graph representations in `docs/workflow-ownership.md`, including the failures owner, and add `src/failures/` to the `CONTRIBUTING.md` code map. Describe current behavior in the present tense without adding a new guide or historical section. Check related references for stale helper paths.

## Step 5 — Validate preservation and prepare review evidence

From the repository root under Node 26.13.0, run `npm run lint:dependencies`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, and `npm run validate -- --skip test:mutation`. Resolve failures attributable to the change and record outcomes; do not claim validation that was not completed.

Verify that `git grep -n -E "export (async )?function (messageOf|rootCause|retryResult)" src` finds exports only under failures. Verify that `git grep -n "from '.*failures/" src/domain src/ports src/config src/prompts` finds nothing. Confirm `src/ports/retry.ts` and `src/ports/exception-details.ts` do not exist, no compatibility exports remain, helper test cases are preserved, and container changes are limited to imports. Inspect the final diff for unrelated edits and behavior changes.

Prepare the eventual PR explanation naming failures as the technical owner, explaining why existing owners cannot serve all consumers, documenting the returned-Result and terminal-callback reasons for the handwritten retry wrapper, and stating that this is a one-off owner rather than a general utility destination. Explain that error ownership, composition and GitHub restructuring remain separate migrations. Include validation evidence without creating release tags or changing the package version.

slices.title: refactor(failures): own shared message and retry helpers
slices.description: Implements plan steps 1-5. Extract messageOf, rootCause, retryResult and RetryPolicy into the failures owner, migrating all consumers and preserving helper behavior and test cases in one coherent refactor. Keep domain error definitions, classification and transientRetryPolicy in domain with an independent structural type; limit container changes to imports. Enforce the new ownership boundaries through the existing dependency checker and comprehensive runtime and type-only fixtures, preserving existing restrictions and coverage. Update internal rules, architecture, ownership graphs and the contributor code map. Under Node 26.13.0, run affected specs and all prescribed validation, verify exclusive helper exports, forbidden imports, absent compatibility modules and unchanged wiring, and inspect the final diff for unrelated changes. Prepare review evidence explaining the owner choice, returned-Result and terminal-callback requirements for the handwritten retry wrapper, its narrowly scoped purpose and the separate migrations left outside this change. Extraction, migration, enforcement and documentation land together because they establish and verify the same ownership boundary.
